text:
maya: Heads up — nightly evals show a spike in nondeterministic failures on the 'kb-recall' prompt set (model=redwood-v2q, quant=4bit). Looks correlated with sampling changes from last deploy. anyone around?

reza: On it. Which metric spiked?

maya: failure_rate went from 1.2% -> 6.8%, and variance in BLEU-like score increased a lot. eval-bot: nightly-eval report attached: run_id=2026-03-08-03, seed_stats: mean_entropy +0.9, top_k median dropped from 40->12 (we log sampled topk distribution).

jon: Wait — top_k median dropped? We didn't touch top_k config in model code. We did change RNG seeding semantics in the sampler last week (deterministic default for multi-request batching). Could be that.

reza: I pushed that change (randstate pooling) — it made batching deterministic across GPU shards. Intent was to reduce jitter. Might have clamped probabilities in edge cases, effectively lowering topk during noisy timesteps.

maya: Attached a short excerpt of failing generations. Many are overly conservative (short, safe answers).

maya: ```
# example prompt id: kb-441
Q: How many satellites are currently in the Galileo constellation?
Expected: ~20
Gen A: I think there are a lot.
Gen B: There are dozens of satellites.
```

jon: That looks like lower entropy sampling. Two hypotheses: 1) seeding change caused correlated streams leading to effective lower temp; 2) interaction with quantized logits -> rounding + clamp.

ci-bot: CI note: the randstate change landed in commit 18f4b2 on 2026-03-06; rollout to canary on 03-07.

reza: I can run ablation: revert randstate pooling locally and run the same nightly eval prompts with exact same seeds.

maya: Please also try bumping temperature + top_p to see if we can recover pass rate; that'll tell us if it's purely sampling scale.

reza: Running small experiment now: configs tried: (a) current commit, temp=0.7 top_k=12 top_p=0.9; (b) revert seeding, temp=0.7 top_k=12 top_p=0.9; (c) current commit, temp=1.2 top_k=40 top_p=0.95. Will post results shortly.

jon: Add a run with float32 logits (no quant) if possible — to check quantization effects. 

maya: Good. Also capture the RNG states used (randstate id) and seed per-thread — we recently started persisting global randstate id in logs but not per-request seed.

eval-bot: quick results (small sample 500 prompts):
- (a) current: pass_rate 0.892, mean_entropy 2.3
- (b) revert seeding: pass_rate 0.978, mean_entropy 3.1
- (c) current + higher temp/topk: pass_rate 0.975, mean_entropy 3.0
- (d) float32 logits (current): pass_rate 0.976, mean_entropy 3.05

maya: OK that pretty much narrows it. Reverting seeding restores behavior; increasing temp/topk also compensates; float32 shows quant is not the primary cause. So the randstate pooling is the culprit.

jon: That suggests our pooled RNG is producing less diverse samples when used across batched shards — maybe because we reuse the same stream offset per sample. We intended independent substreams.

reza: I dug into the code: we were assigning the same base rng and advancing by batch_count * max_steps rather than per-sequence offsets. Fix is straightforward (use per-sample offset derived from unique request id). I'll open a PR to change the offset math and add a test that checks sampled top_k distribution matches pre-change.

maya: Nice. Can we also add an eval regression guard in nightly that compares KL of sampling distribution and throws a warning if KL > threshold? This would catch future sampling semantics changes.

jon: Agreed — add a quick Kv: store a small fingerprint of top_k histogram across a fixed prompt shard and compare.

reza: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampler/pull/291 — patch fixes per-sample offset and adds unit tests + an integration job that runs 1k prompts with fixed randseed.

ci-bot: Build passed on PR 291, canary deploy scheduled for 2026-03-09T02:15Z.

maya: After canary, let's run full nightly eval and confirm regression resolved. Also add note to release changelog warning about 'randstate pooling impact on sampling diversity' so future debugging is easier.

jon: I'll add the KL/regression check to the nightly eval harness. Maybe we record median top_k and entropy per-run.

maya: Thanks all. Learned: sampling determinism changes can reduce diversity in subtle ways — always compare sampled-stat fingerprints after such infra changes. :memo: :mag:
